title.en: Diagonals and points equidistant from two points

text.en:
Meena drew the diagonals of a rectangle and found they crossed at the middle.
"They are equal and bisect each other," she said.

A diagonal joins opposite corners. The diagonals of a rectangle are equal and cut each other in half. In a square they also cross at right angles.
Points that are the same distance from two given points lie on a special line called the perpendicular bisector of the line joining them.
We can draw it with a compass: draw arcs of equal radius from both points and join the places where they cross.

problem.en: Where do points equidistant from A and B lie?

text.en: They are equally far from A and B.
They lie on the perpendicular bisector.
That line cuts AB in half at a right angle.

prompt.en: A friend says diagonals of a rectangle are always unequal. How will you reply?

points.en: Equidistant points lie on the perpendicular bisector.
